messages:
mira: Heads-up — the structured-output CI started failing only for the AWQ-int8 runner when we enable batching. Single-request/native streaming runs are fine. Failures look like JSON getting wrapped into a string or arrays losing their brackets.

mira: Minimal repro (same prompt/seed):
```bash
# run with batch processing turned on
./awq_runner --model ./models/xyz_awq_int8.bin --batch-size 8 --seed 42 --prompt-file tests/structured_prompts.jsonl --output-format json

# run single-request (no batching)
./awq_runner --model ./models/xyz_awq_int8.bin --batch-size 1 --seed 42 --prompt-file tests/structured_prompts.jsonl --output-format json
```

mira: Example single-request output (valid):
```json
{"id": "t1", "tools": [{"name":"lookup","args": {"q":"foo"}}]}
```

mira: Example batched output (broken):
```json
{"id": "t1", "tools": "[{\"name\":\"lookup\",\"args\": {\"q\":\"foo\"}}]"}
```

alex: whoa. same tokenizer/config both runs? looks like some decode path is adding literal quotes around the emitted array. any diffs in decode options (clean_up_tokenization_spaces / skip_special_tokens)?

mira: yep same binary and same cli flags. base decode args: skip_special_tokens=true, normalize=true. I double-checked the prompt bytes and seeds. Only difference is batch-size and the runtime turning on continuous batching and padding to max len.

samir: this smells like a padding/concat boundary issue where the batched decoder inserts an extra escape or a surrogate token at sequence boundaries. maybe the code that joins completed sequences treats some outputs as partial and wraps them as raw str. i've seen similar when the sampler flushes KV cache mid-token.

zoya: can you run the failing batch but force no-pad / pad-with-eos? also try disabling any post-process that collapses multiple chunks. if the bug is in the post-join logic it should show up in the chunk logs.

mira: tried pad-with-eos and disabling chunk-collapse. still reproduces. Quick stats from the structured-output smoke suite (200 samples):
- AWQ-int8 batch (batch-size 8): 73/200 valid json and schema-validated
- AWQ-int8 single (batch-size 1): 198/200 valid
- FP8 binary batch: 194/200 valid

mira: note: the 73 valid ones look like short responses that don't cross the pad boundary. failures correlate with longer outputs that go across the internal buffer flush.

samir: ok that nails it being a cross-boundary flush/continuation bug. possibilities:
- chunk concatenation is injecting an extra leading quote before bracket chars for certain tokenization boundaries
- tokenizer special tokens mapped to printable chars in int8 path (weird mapping)
- sampling/temperature differences under batched micro-batches that cause the model to output a leading '\"' as its first token for that chunk

alex: do we see this with GPTQ or other quantization profiles? if not, maybe AWQ's remapping + runtime's chunk join interplay is the culprit.

mira: quick matrix I ran locally (200 samples each):
- AWQ-int8 batched: 73/200
- AWQ-int8 single: 198/200
- GPTQ-int8 batched: 189/200
- FP8 batched: 194/200
So it's primarily AWQ batched mode.

quant-bot: automated-results: job https://ci.redwood/inference/quant-suite/4821 — AWQ-int8-batched failed 62% of structured-output checks, artifacts at s3://redwood-qa/4821/

infra-ci: CI job 4821 captured full stdout+chunk logs: https://ci.redwood/logs/4821. we have the per-chunk token ids for each sample.

samir: next steps I suggest:
1) add an assert in the chunk-joiner that verifies the first char of continuation chunks is not an unmatched quote/bracket unless previous chunk ended with an escape. log token ids around the boundary.
2) run a micro-batch reproducer that forces many chunk boundaries (max_seq_len small) to speed bisect.
3) diff tokenizer outputs (ids -> bytes) between AWQ and FP8 for failing samples.

mira: on it. i'll push a reproducer that runs batch-size=8 but sets max_seq_len=32 so every output crosses a chunk boundary. will upload token dumps to the CI artifacts and ping here.

zoya: also try toggling "disable_continuous_batching=true" in the runtime routing (we saw different behavior in earlier optimizations). if that fixes it, we can hold a quick rollback for the batching glue while we bisect AWQ changes.

mira: thanks — reproducer + token dumps uploaded: s3://redwood-qa/4821/awq-chunk-dumps.tar.gz. i'll open a bug and include sample ids.

alex: filed INF-1219 referencing the CI job and attaching a small set of failing examples. tagging runtime and awq teams.

mira: tagging @samir @zoya for follow-up. will post a short summary after the bisect. :white_check_mark:

quant-bot: INF-1219 created and linked to job 4821.

mira: thanks all, moving to bisect now.
